# PadNote

> Open-source Android tablet notes: write or annotate a PDF, select a passage, ask your configured AI service, and keep useful explanations on the page. A computer agent is optional.

## Install and status

- Repository: https://github.com/shiyan688/padnote
- Published Android download: v0.18.0-beta.13, debug-signed test APK; minimum Android 7.0 / API 24.
- Download: https://github.com/shiyan688/padnote/releases/tag/v0.18.0-beta.13
- iPad: source is available; build and sign with Xcode. There is no signed, installable IPA.
- First-use UI improvements in the current source revision are not included in the published beta.13 APK.
- The optional Windows connection assistant uses the beta.11 installer. It is not required for ordinary notes or direct AI explanations.

## First useful workflow

1. Create a note, or import a PDF and annotate it.
2. Lasso a small area and inspect the AI card selection preview.
3. Configure an HTTPS OpenAI-compatible endpoint, an image-capable model and your own API key.
4. Choose Allow note edits or Only card, then Explain; confirm the material and destination before sending.
5. Check the explanation and save the note. AI writes associated with a PDF go to blank annotation pages.

## Scope and costs

- Writing and local notes do not require a model account. AI requires a configured remote service.
- PadNote does not provide model credits. Availability, usage fees and provider terms depend on the chosen service.
- Android model requests use the selected image, question/conversation context and a layout map without note text. Additional Markdown knowledge-base material must be explicitly selected.
- Read scope and permission to write into the note are separate. Model tools cannot modify handwriting.
- Answers are non-streaming. Local cancellation does not guarantee that the provider stopped processing or billing.
- Notes are local by default. There is no automatic cloud sync.
- Optional Share / Agent tasks can be sent to a paired Hermes target that supports paper context. OpenClaw currently offers discovery/setup guidance; Codex paper tasks are not connected.
- The desktop assistant does not bundle Hermes, model credentials, or a video runtime.

## Verification and licensing

The beta.13 report records 329 JVM tests and Android API 35 emulator UI checks. That round did not test a physical tablet, real model requests, or real agent requests. These historical results are not verification of later source changes; consult the corresponding test report.

Original Android/iPad code uses MIT. The video Agent subproject uses Apache-2.0. Third-party components retain their own licenses.
